mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (measured as the 3-month change) compresses discount rates and increases equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 5.0%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that reduces corporate earnings growth and increases equity risk premiums, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in < 40% of triggered instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and residential fixed investment (RSAFS) signals a deteriorating housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic slowdown and negative equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS decline by > 3% in the last 3 months
failure_condition: HOUST and RSAFS decline by > 3% in the last 3 months but SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100 (the 2017 base level), it signals a contraction in the real economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 100 but SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of such instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of high labor market tightness (defined as UNRATE < 4.5% and 3-month PAYEMS growth > 0.5%), the economy is in a late-cycle expansion phase, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: High labor market tightness conditions are met but SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of such instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPI (CPIAUCSL) index rises to 202.0 or above, it signals persistent inflation, prompting central bank tightening and negative equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL >= 202.0 but SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of such instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.5% over the last 3 months and a CPIAUCSL index above 202.0 signals an aggressive monetary tightening cycle, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS 3-month change > 0.5% and CPIAUCSL > 202.0 but SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of such instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (measured as the 3-month change) signals a contraction in the real economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in contraction periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
